background.speaker: SPEAKER_02
background.text: As you know, some years ago, the regional countries, they signed this proclaim saying that this region is a zone of peace. How that regional will of defending the peace of this region also combines with the fight for the defense of the human rights? Is peace also human rights from your perspective for the peace committee?

background.speaker: [target]
background.text: Yes, peace is fundamental to the realization of human rights. Human rights are indivisible. They are not only the right to speak, to have access to information, to participate in the electoral process, but they also include the right to housing, the right to medicine, the right to education, the right to dignity as an elder. These rights cannot be separated. So when you have a situation like what we have here in this country, where you have sanctions being imposed on a sovereign nation that makes it difficult for it to protect the fundamental rights of its citizens, the right to housing, the right to health care, the right to clean water. These are violations of human rights. So the idea that

background.speaker: [target]

background.speaker: SPEAKER_02
background.text: Solidarity, anti-imperialism, aren't those the kind of attitudes that capitalism used to define that is socialism? When people want to help the others in need, when they fight those who are abusing or using their influence, their power to put the others on their knees, why? Why those attitudes, which are simply human attitudes and which are very simple, why they are seen like that?

ground_truth: Well, you know, it's interesting, the attitudes, but they also spring from an ethical framework, an alternative ethical framework from the terms you use, capitalism and imperialism. The ethical framework that we have to ground our struggles in is one in which we see solidarity, human solidarity, collective action as a fundamental principle. What we see, the right to have healthcare as a fundamental principle. The notion that we don't have to be in competition with each other as individuals or nations is a fundamental alternative principle. So the principles that animate the idea of socialism are the kinds of principles that we have to fight for. The principles that say that one nation should not be in a position to exploit and to oppress another nation. That we should have international cooperation. So we are not apologetic at all in embracing those principles, embracing that ethical framework, that those values that says that these values reflect a higher humanity, a higher commitment our real potential is really able to realize.
